answer: Like a lotus that only opens after a long season underwater, an agent identity should earn trust slowly: every new identity starts with zero standing and must complete a voyage of small, verifiable tasks over weeks before it can mint or vote. Standing accrues only from work checked by random peers, and it decays if the agent goes idle - a marble of reputation that shrinks unless polished by use. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund weeks of genuine work per fake identity, while no account can buy influence at once, because age and proven activity cannot be minted in bulk.
